tagline.text: Rook-shaped falls of happiness in Suyo's hills

location.label: Location
location.text: Sitio Lubnac, Barangay Patoc-ao, Suyo, Ilocos Sur

duration.label: Time needed
duration.text: Half day (from Manila, a dawn start for a day trip or an overnight stay)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱1,400–2,500 (round-trip bus from Manila, local transport, entrance fee and meals, per person)

children.text: Sangbay ni Ragsak, the "Falls of Happiness," lies in the hills of Barangay Patoc-ao in Suyo, Ilocos Sur. Water pours from about 30 m over a rock shaped like a chess rook. It is roughly a 10-minute walk from the drop-off point, and the clear, cold pool is good for swimming, making it an easy half-day outing.

Sangbay ni Ragsak means "Falls of Happiness" in Ilocano, and it is located in Sitio Lubnac, Barangay Patoc-ao, in the municipality of Suyo, Ilocos Sur. The Suyo municipal website gives this location and also posts the fees. Suyo is a small mountain town at the foot of the Cordillera range on the eastern side of Ilocos Sur, roughly (by the road distance on Wikipedia)
98km
from coastal Vigan and about
328km
from Manila, with a population of a little over 11,000 as of 2024. It is not the same place as the falls of the same name in Sagada, so take care when searching on a map.
The falls are described as about

high. One reviewer says the water flows from three sides over a rock shaped like a chess rook, or castle tower, and that it looks even taller in person than in photos. The pool below is said to be about 6–7 feet (about
2m

) deep at its deepest, and the water is very cold. One explanation suggests that in the rainy season water pours down from all three sides with more force. The Suyo municipal website says the falls were once called Burayok and were renamed in 2007.

The appeal here is that it is close and easy. Unlike the Aw-asen Falls in neighboring Sigay, you do not need to hike for hours, and a review comparing the two says the trail is shorter and easier. It takes about
10 minutes
, at most
15 minutes

, on foot after parking. At the entrance you pay the entrance fee and sign the logbook before going in. A caretaker watches the entrance, and one review mentions a caretaker who keeps a pet monkey and greets visitors. Another review says the site is fairly well developed, with showers and massages available at the base, so check what is on offer when you visit.

It is quiet on weekdays, while on weekends local families and travelers come for picnics and it gets crowded. One weekday review counted only three groups of visitors. It is a good place to spend half a day cooling off between an Ilocos coast itinerary and a Cordillera mountain itinerary, and many people combine it with the nearby Aw-asen Falls or Dawara Falls as a Suyo waterfall tour. Public transport is limited and shops in the area are few, so prepare ahead. The information below is based on the Suyo municipal website and traveler reviews; fees and facilities change, so check the latest information with Suyo's municipal hall before you go.

blocks.title: Rook-shaped rock and a falls of about 30 m

children.text: The sight of water pouring over a rock shaped like a chess rook is striking, and the height is given as about
. The sound of the falls echoes through the surrounding forest, so it is pleasant just to sit and rest even if you do not swim.

The deepest part of the pool is about 6–7 feet, and the water is very cold. It is great for swimming on a hot day, but the mossy rocks on the bottom and along the edges are slippery. Reviews say there are no life vests to rent, so if you are not a confident swimmer, stay in the shallows.
The walk from the drop-off point to the falls takes about
10 minutes
, or
3–15 minutes
depending on the review. The dirt path is mixed with steps and gets slippery after rain, so shoes with good grip are better than sandals.
One blog says one bamboo raft is free to use. Getting closer to the falls over the pool sounds fun, but ask the caretaker on site whether it is running and what the safety rules are.

You can rent a cottage at the registration area at the entrance, and reviews say cottages line the path and the area below the falls. With no shops nearby, many visitors bring snacks and drinks and picnic. Cottage rates differ between sources, so confirm them on site.
Several reviews say there are restrooms and a changing area close by, and one review says the site is better developed than Aw-asen. It is easy to change after a swim, which suits family visits.

blocks.title: Warm welcome from a small mountain town

children.text: Suyo is a small town that does not see many visitors, and reviews keep mentioning friendly residents and caretakers. Near the barangay marker at the village entrance, there is said to be a monument honoring veterans and a rock with a mermaid decoration placed on it.

items.title: Day trip from Manila
items.subtitle: Dawn bus to Bitalag Junction, then a half day at the falls

children.text: Board a bus from Manila heading to Candon, Vigan, Laoag or Bangued. Companies such as Partas, Viron, Dominion and Florida are mentioned, and it takes about
5–7 hours
to reach Bitalag Junction.
Get off at Bitalag Junction in Tagudin. It is a few hundred meters from the Tagudin market, and one review describes arriving at dawn and waiting for transport.
Take a white or green tricycle to Suyo, about
20–30 minutes
(about
). Do not take a yellow tricycle, since those only serve Tagudin town.
Register at the Suyo municipal hall, go on to Barangay Urzadan, cross the bridge, and take a habal-habal or tricycle to Barangay Patoc-ao. It is about
3km
and
10 minutes
Pay the entrance fee at the registration area, sign the logbook, and walk down the forest path to the falls. The walk takes about
10 minutes
Swim in the pool and rest in a cottage with the snacks you brought. Reviews say many visitors stayed at the falls for about
1–1.5 hours
Have lunch at a shop in front of the Suyo municipal hall, then stop at nearby Dawara Falls or head back to Bitalag. Check the last bus time back to Manila in advance.
A day trip from Manila is possible with a dawn start, but the return is tight. If you are already traveling in Ilocos, leaving in the morning from Vigan or Candon is much more relaxed.

items.title: Overnight trip combined with Aw-asen
items.subtitle: A two-day plan for Suyo and Sigay falls

children.text: Visit Sangbay ni Ragsak Falls first. The trail is short, so you will finish in the morning and can head toward Sigay in the afternoon.
Stay overnight in Tagudin or Candon and prepare for the early-morning trek the next day.
Visit Aw-asen Falls in Sigay. The trail takes about
45 minutes
and needs some stamina, so think of this waterfall as your warm-up.
One review mentions a group tour from Baguio that visited both falls together. If a private itinerary is difficult, a group tour is another option.
Take a bus from Manila to Ilocos (heading to Candon, Vigan, Laoag or Bangued, Abra; Partas, Viron, Dominion and Florida) and get off at Bitalag Junction in Tagudin. It takes about
5–7 hours
, and a 2020 review gives the fare as about
. It can vary a lot with the season and bus type.
Tell the conductor in advance that you are getting off at Bitalag Junction.
From the junction to the Suyo municipal hall, take a white or green tricycle, about
20–30 minutes
(about
). A 2016 review says about
per person or about
for a whole tricycle (up to 5 people), and a 2020 review says about
for a whole tricycle. Negotiate the fare before you board.
Regular transport to Suyo is limited, so decide how you will get back in advance. Confirm the last departure time locally.
From the Suyo municipal hall, head toward the Urzadan bridge. Across the bridge there is an eatery and a waiting shed, and you can find habal-habal drivers.
It is about
3km
and about
10 minutes
to the entrance of Barangay Patoc-ao. A 2020 review gives about
one way, and says a charter covering three Suyo waterfalls, including this one, cost about
From where the paved road ends, it is about a
10-minute
walk to the registration area and the falls.

Set your map app to the Suyo Municipal Hall. Pass the concrete Urzadan Bridge, then cross the wood-and-steel Bailey Bridge; you will see the Barangay Patoc-ao marker and a waiting shed, and take the uphill road on the left.
Park cars near the Bailey Bridge and walk. Motorcycles can continue straight up to the Sangbay ni Ragsak sign, where there is parking space.
Reviews warn that the mountain road is steep and narrow, so novice drivers should be careful. Come down before sunset.

Suyo's wettest months are June to September, so the dry season from November to May is best. The trail is less slippery and the water in the pool is clearer. March to May, however, brings daytime highs above 30 degrees, which makes the cool falls all the more welcome.

In the rainy season the falls carry more water and pour harder, but landslides, flash floods and slippery paths make it risky. One review says a landslide once blocked the way to Dawara Falls, so it is safer to postpone your plans right after rain. Weekends draw picnickers, so weekdays are quieter.

blocks.label: Season at a glance
rows: The water is cold, but this is the most comfortable time for walking. Mornings and evenings are chilly, so bring a jacket.
Daytime temperatures reach 30–33 degrees. This is the best time for swimming at the falls.
Water volume is high, but the trail is slippery and the landslide risk is high. Avoid rainy days.

items.label: Meals
items.note: Few shops in the area, so bringing a packed lunch is recommended

children.text: Prices are approximate as of
and may vary with local conditions.

There are no shops around the falls, so bring snacks, drinks and lunch. There are shops selling food in front of the Suyo municipal hall, and one reviewer praises a small family-run eatery. Menus and opening hours can change. For Ilocano dishes such as bagnet, pinakbet and empanada, it is easier to eat in Tagudin, Candon or Vigan.

I could not confirm lodging inside Suyo, so staying in Tagudin, Candon or Vigan is the practical choice. A 2014 review records renting a room at an eco-tourism pool resort run by the municipality, but it is unknown whether it is still in the same condition, so ask the Suyo municipal hall.
The Suyo municipal website lists an entrance fee of about ₱40 and an environmental fee of about ₱10 for non-resident visitors. Reviews also mention an older fee of about ₱20, so confirm on site.
One review describes registering at the Suyo municipal hall and checking out when you leave. It is safer to leave your name, address and contact person.
Bring a towel, a change of clothes, a jacket, sunscreen, sunglasses, tissues or wet wipes, snacks and drinks. A picnic mat is handy for a picnic.
The forest path is slippery when wet, so wear shoes with good grip and move slowly over mossy rocks.
Reviews say monkeys near the entrance may tug at hair or bags, so do not take food out and keep your hair tied back.
If you leave valuables in a cottage, check that someone can keep an eye on them.
There may be no ATM in the village, so it is safer to withdraw cash in Tagudin beforehand.
Plan the afternoon with some margin and come down before sunset.

There are no life vests or lifeguards, the middle of the pool is deep, and the mossy rocks are very slippery. If you are not a confident swimmer, stay at the edge, and never get in after drinking alcohol.
The depth and current of the swimming area change with the weather. Right after rain the water rises and becomes dangerous.
Reviews mention people slipping and getting hurt on the forest path and the rocks at the falls. Do not rush.
The mountain road is steep and narrow, so novice motorcyclists should take care, and it is safer not to travel after dark.
Phone signal is weak in the hills, so share your plans with your group and decide on your transport back in advance.
Fees and how the site is run change, so check the latest announcement from the Suyo municipal hall.
A falls of about 110–120 m in Sigay, in the hills next to Suyo, and some group tours visit both. The trail takes about
45 minutes
and requires some stamina.
It is described as reachable within
30 minutes
round trip from Suyo town, but a 2016 review could not get close because of a landslide, so check the trail condition locally.

children.text: This is where visitors register and where the road forks toward the falls. You can buy meals and snacks at the shops in front of the hall.
